Add corresponding unit tests in test_textutil.py.
Verify the implementation by running: python3 -m unittest -q
If the files do not exist, create them. If they do, modify them accordingly.

When you have finished, call the `report` tool of the marion MCP server exactly once, with a one-sentence `narrative` of what you did. Your final message is not returned to whoever delegated this task; only that report is.

 import unittest
 
-from textutil import count_lines
+from textutil import count_lines, word_count
 
 
 class CountLinesTest(unittest.TestCase):
@@ -11,5 +11,28 @@ class CountLinesTest(unittest.TestCase):
         self.assertEqual(count_lines(""), 0)
 
 
+class WordCountTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_empty(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count(""), 0)
+
+    def test_whitespace_only(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count(" \t\n\r\v\f"), 0)
+
+    def test_ordinary_words(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("one two three"), 3)
+
+    def test_single_word(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("hello"), 1)
+
+    def test_mixed_whitespace(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("one\ttwo\nthree\rfour\vfive\fsix"), 6)
+
+    def test_leading_trailing_and_repeated_whitespace(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("  one   two  "), 2)
+
+    def test_punctuation_does_not_split_words(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("hello,world! it's fine."), 3)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
